name: SpaceX Starship V3 (Super Heavy 33×Raptor 3 + Ship 3 SL + 3 vac Raptor 3) — TIMELINE mode

diameter_m.note: 9 m diameter; Wikipedia cites SpaceX 'Introducing Starship V3' (12 May 2026) / technical specifications

propellant_kg.note: Block 3 / V3 propellant mass 3,650 t (8,050,000 lb). Wikipedia cites SpaceX technical specifications / Introducing Starship V3 (12 May 2026). The SpaceX specs page is JS-only and was not scraped this turn; figure taken from the cited Wikipedia infobox.

dry_kg.assumption: Super Heavy V3 empty mass unpublished. 275 t is the earlier-block empty mass on the same Wikipedia Super Heavy infobox (gross 3,675 t with 3,400 t propellant). Used as a labelled stand-in, NOT a V3 measurement.

thrust_sl_N.note: 80.8 MN / 8,240 tf liftoff thrust, 33× Raptor 3, cited to SpaceX specs / Introducing Starship V3

thrust_vac_N.assumption: vacuum increment for the 33 sea-level Raptor 3s is unpublished; SL/liftoff thrust is used at all altitudes (Ae=0), which slightly understates high-altitude thrust

isp_vac_s.assumption: Raptor 3 Isp is widely reported as 350 s from SpaceX's August 2024 Raptor 3 reveal; a primary transcript was not retrieved this turn. Treated as an ASSUMPTION.

ignition_s.note: SpaceX Flight 15 mission API / page: Liftoff T+00:00:00 (content.spacex.com/api/spacex-website/missions/starship-flight-15)

cutoff_s.note: SpaceX F15 post-launch timeline: Super Heavy MECO (most engines cut off) T+00:02:19

separation_s.note: SpaceX F15: Hot-staging (Starship Raptor ignition and stage separation) T+00:02:21. Unburned Super Heavy residual stands in for the unpublished boostback/landing reserve (boostback T+2:26–3:02, landing burn T+6:10–6:35, not modelled).

propellant_kg.note: Block 3 ship propellant 1,600 t, Wikipedia citing Musk / SpaceX V3 materials. Same caveat as the booster: specs page not scraped this turn.

dry_kg.assumption: Starship V3 dry mass unpublished. Elon Musk in 2021 quoted ~100 t for a much earlier ship. 120 t is a labelled stand-in for a V3 ship, NOT a measurement.

thrust_vac_N.note: Block 3 'Ship initial thrust' 1,600 tf. Flight 14 narrative: ship ignites all six Raptors on ascent (3 sea-level + 3 vacuum). 1,600 tf ≈ 3×250 tf SL + 3×275 tf vac (1,575 tf) plus a small official rounding.

thrust_sl_N.assumption: hot-stage start is already above the atmosphere; vac thrust used

isp_vac_s.assumption: same Raptor 3 350 s ASSUMPTION as the booster; mix of SL and vacuum bells would have a slightly higher blend-average, unpublished

ignition_s.note: F15 hot-staging / Starship Raptor ignition T+00:02:21

cutoff_s.note: F15 Starship engine cutoff T+00:08:09 (ascent burn). Orbital insertion burn is a later restart (T+26:10–26:30) and is modelled in post_cutoff, not in this cutoff.

mass_kg.assumption: no jettisoned payload fairing; Starlink V3 stack is carried internally and deployed through a door. Mass 0 so the jettison event is a no-op.

jettison_time_s.assumption: dummy time at staging; fairing mass is 0

cd.assumption: not published; generic Cd. A 9 m cylinder would have a different (unpublished) coefficient; not fitted.

payload_kg.basis: 26 Starlink V3 satellites, mass unpublished by SpaceX. NSF unofficial 44–52 t is NOT used as a source. Fitted payload is NOT an estimate of the real stack.

header_notes: Starship V3: Super Heavy 3,650 t propellant, 33× Raptor 3, 80.8 MN / 8,240 tf liftoff; Ship Block 3 1,600 t propellant, 1,600 tf initial thrust (Wikipedia citing SpaceX 'Introducing Starship V3' / technical specifications, 12 May 2026). V3 dry masses and Raptor 3 Isp are ASSUMED (see fields).

TIMELINE mode uses SpaceX's published Flight 15 event times (content.spacex.com/api/spacex-website/missions/starship-flight-15, also spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-15): MECO 139 s, hot-stage / ship ignition 141 s, ship ascent cutoff 489 s. Boostback and catch are not modelled; unburned booster propellant stands in for the recovery reserve.

The 20 s orbital insertion burn (T+26:10–26:30) and payload deploy (start 35:01, complete 1:17:40) are flown in post_cutoff. SpaceX: ~275 km, ~14 orbits, >22-hour flight, then RTLS catch if the vehicle is healthy.
